title: Order decline at Riverbend Pharma Distributors (Fictional) 4704
silent_period_basis: Days from estimated onset until a weekly manual review of order totals would flag it (assumption: flags a >25% month-on-month drop).

evidence.label: Complaints
evidence.caption: How many more complaints this account raised than it normally does in four weeks. Note that fewer orders with more complaints means the experience got worse, not just busier.
evidence.definition: Count of complaints (kinds: service, delivery, billing) in the last 4 weeks vs baseline. COUNT, not rate: this is what deck slide 7 shows ('Complaints up 47%').

evidence.label: Overdue receivables
evidence.caption: How much of what this account owes us is late. Paired with falling orders it suggests the customer is under financial stress.
evidence.definition: Overdue (>0 days past due) outstanding / trailing 12-week billing.

evidence.label: Order volume
evidence.caption: How much less (or more) this account bought recently than its own normal. A drop alone is weak; a drop with other signals is a pattern.
evidence.definition: Units ordered, last 4 weeks vs baseline weekly mean x 4, as fractional change.

evidence.label: Order value
evidence.caption: Same idea as volume but in rupees, so a mix shift to cheaper products shows up.
evidence.definition: Order value (INR), same windows as order_volume_delta.

steps.summary: Incident INC-2026-0002: high, risk 78, 3 source systems (finance, orders, support).

Retrieved 5 similar records with TF-IDF; best INC-018 (similarity 0.562).
Drafted a 8-step plan from SOP-04 and INC-018; requires Business Head.

narrative.text: Sentinel found 3 independent source systems moving together: Complaints +125% vs this account's own normal; Overdue receivables at 81% of trailing 12-week billing; Order volume -16% vs this account's own normal; Order value -19% vs this account's own normal.
Overdue receivables above normal: Overdue receivables at 81% of trailing 12-week billing.
Order volume falling: Order volume -16% vs this account's own normal.
Complaints up: Complaints +125% vs this account's own normal.
The cause rule that fits best is payment stress; the customer-side symptoms follow from it rather than from a demand change.
Organizational memory's closest match is INC-018 (Chemist chain payment delays after its own funding squeeze), resolved by: Credit hold after stalled payment negotiation.

steps.action: Review receivables ageing and current credit exposure
Contact the account to understand the cause of delay
Propose a payment plan with a reduced credit limit
Decide on payment plan or credit hold
Apply the decided order release rule in operations
Escalate overdue balance to finance and business head
Place the account on credit hold
Negotiate recovery of the overdue balance
